minutes.headline: Select Board voted 3-2 to pull the APDC/Historical Commission merger article from the special town meeting warrant
minutes.summary: The Select Board spent most of a long meeting on a contentious proposal to merge the Architectural Preservation District Commission into the Historical Commission for the November 18th special town meeting, hearing extensive public opposition and legal analysis from town counsel before voting 3-2 to remove it from the warrant. The board also closed two utility pole hearings, approved an earth removal permit, and worked through the rest of the special town meeting warrant, deferring the noise ordinance article and voting to include and recommend approval of the 41A senior tax deferral and special education reserve fund articles.

watch_next: Board meets Friday at 4 p.m. to finalize the special town meeting warrant, then again November 4th
Special town meeting, November 18 at 7 p.m., where the finalized warrant goes to voters

what_happened.line: Select Board voted 3-2 to pull the APDC/Historical Commission merger article from the special town meeting warrant.
The vote followed extended public opposition and a town counsel review of legal questions the merger raised.
The board voted 4-1 to recommend the special education reserve fund article, after a member flagged a possible hidden future budget impact.
The noise ordinance article was deferred and will not appear on this warrant, pending further work.
The board voted to include and recommend the 41A senior tax deferral article, raising the decades-old income threshold for that exemption.

why_it_matters: Pulling the merger article means the Architectural Preservation District Commission keeps separate authority over historic-district reviews, at least until a future town meeting takes it up again.
The 41A article, if approved by voters at the November 18 special town meeting, would let more senior homeowners qualify to defer their property tax bills.
The special education reserve fund article changes how the town could set aside money for special-ed costs; it carries no budget impact yet, but a member noted it could down the road.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: Every non-procedural vote (all 10), the numeric substance of nearly every figure, and the key warrant-article decisions agree between the two records — most differences are caption mishearings of names and digits, not substance. The two things a reader should actually check are the article-letter mix-up on the $50,000 project-estimator funding (G vs. H) and whether Article F's cemetery transfer got a fresh vote at this meeting or was only recapped, since ours implies a vote and the official minutes say it was "previously voted."
